ABOUT THE ROLE
The Senior Software Engineer - Developer Experience is a hands-on individual contributor focused on improving how engineers build, test, and deliver software across Genesys. You will design and deliver scalable tooling, automation, and development workflows that reduce friction, increase delivery velocity, and improve software quality. You will also help advance Genesys's AI-enabled software development lifecycle (AI-SDLC), applying sound technical judgment as AI capabilities and engineering practices evolve. This role has no direct reports; you will lead through technical ownership, mentorship, and collaboration.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Developer Experience & Platforms
· Design and deliver internal developer platforms, CI/CD pipelines, and reusable tooling that streamline code development, testing, and deployment workflows.
· Build and improve standardized development environments and paved workflows using GitHub, CI/CD automation, and testing frameworks to reduce setup time and inconsistencies across partner teams.
· Improve developer onboarding and day-to-day productivity by creating self-service capabilities, documentation, and paved paths for common engineering tasks.

AI-SDLC, Automation & Quality
· Implement and continuously improve AI-enabled software development practices, evaluating emerging capabilities and incorporating effective approaches into development, testing, and delivery workflows while maintaining quality, security, and reliability.
· Automate build, test, and release processes across the software development lifecycle to reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and shorten delivery cycles.
· Use software delivery and quality metrics, including build success rates, test effectiveness, lead time, deployment frequency, and change failure rate, to identify bottlenecks, prioritize improvements, and measure impact.

Engineering Delivery & Adoption
· Contribute to technical design and reusable frameworks for developer tooling and platforms, balancing developer usability, scalability, security, and operational reliability.
· Partner with platform, security, and application teams to deliver developer experience improvements aligned with enterprise standards and engineering needs, and support adoption by gathering feedback and iterating based on usage and impact.
· Mentor engineers through code and design reviews, pairing, and knowledge sharing to strengthen engineering practices within the team and partner teams.

WHAT YOU BRING
Required Qualifications
· Demonstrated understanding of how AI is changing software development, with the ability to evaluate emerging tools and practices, learn rapidly as capabilities evolve, and apply effective approaches to engineering workflows.
· Strong hands-on software engineering experience using Python, Java, or another modern programming language, with demonstrated experience designing and delivering production-quality software or developer tooling.
· Experience in developer productivity, DevOps, or platform engineering, with a track record of delivering complex technical initiatives and contributing to cross-team efforts.
· Strong experience with CI/CD systems, version control, automated testing frameworks, and cloud-native development environments (preferably AWS) or infrastructure projects.
· Experience using software delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, build reliability, or change failure rate to identify and improve engineering workflows.
· Ability to influence adoption of tools and practices through collaboration, technical judgment, clear communication, and effective partnership across engineering teams.
· Experience with developer infrastructure, observability, and testing technologies such as GitHub, Terraform, Honeycomb, Gremlin, Playwright, or comparable tools.

Preferred Qualifications
· Experience integrating AI-powered developer tools, code assistants, agents, or automation capabilities into engineering workflows.
· Experience working in large-scale SaaS or distributed engineering organizations.
If you bring many of these capabilities but do not meet every qualification listed, we encourage you to apply. We value demonstrated ability, sound engineering judgment, and the capacity to learn as technologies and practices evolve.

KEY SKILLS
· Developer Experience (DevEx)
· CI/CD & Automation
· AI-Enabled Software Development (AI-SDLC)
· Software Quality & Testing
· Technical Design & Collaboration

BUSINESS IMPACT
· Reduces developer friction and cycle time across development, testing, and release workflows through automation, self-service capabilities, and paved paths.
· Improves software delivery and quality indicators such as build reliability, lead time, deployment frequency, and change failure rate within supported engineering workflows.
· Expands effective adoption of standardized and AI-enabled development practices, helping engineering teams use emerging capabilities responsibly while maintaining quality, security, and reliability.

An overview of this role

As an Engineering Manager on GitLab's Authentication team, you'll build and lead a team of engineers in Bangalore who own how users, applications, tokens, and artificial intelligence (AI) agents sign in to GitLab. At GitLab, we see our team as our product. You'll need to be technically credible in authentication protocols such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), and Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML). Your main focus will be hiring well, growing your engineers, and helping the team deliver on commitments that other parts of GitLab depend on. You'll guide your team's work on OAuth across Cells, global identities, token consolidation, and moving authentication out of the Ruby on Rails monolith onto GATE, GitLab's new authentication and authorization platform. You'll manage these multi-quarter programs with fixed deadlines and many dependent teams.

 

What you'll do

  • Hire, onboard, and grow a team of senior and intermediate engineers in Bangalore, working with talent acquisition during a high-volume hiring period.
  • Own delivery for your team's part of the authentication roadmap: plan in milestones, track risks early, and communicate clearly when a date is at risk and what would change it.
  • Work with your Staff Engineer and Product Manager to turn architecture decisions into shippable, feature-flagged increments.
  • Protect your team's focus. Manage requests from other teams through one intake path, and make trade-offs visible to leadership.
  • Coordinate with the GATE Core, GATE Infra, Authorization, and Tenant Scale (Cells and Organizations) teams across India, Europe, and the Americas.
  • Make sure the team runs what it builds, including on-call coverage, incident response for authentication issues, rate limits, and production readiness for new services.
  • Build a team culture where security comes first, decisions are written down, and code review is thorough and kind.
  • Give clear, regular feedback, run career conversations, and handle performance issues early.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you'll bring

  • Significant experience as an engineering manager of backend or platform teams, including hiring and growing senior engineers.
  • A background as an engineer in identity, authentication, or security systems, with enough depth in OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and JSON Web Tokens to review designs and ask probing questions.
  • Experience delivering complex, multi-team programs against fixed dates, including migrations that must not disrupt existing customers.
  • Experience running production services, including on-call coverage, incident response, and reliability work.
  • Working knowledge of Ruby on Rails or Go.
  • Experience building a new team or growing one quickly while keeping the hiring bar high.
  • Clear, concise written English and comfort leading a team in an all-remote, asynchronous company across time zones.

About the team

We're part of the Security Platform stage, alongside Authorization, GATE Core, GATE Infra, Secrets Manager, and other security teams. You'll partner closely with our existing Authentication engineers in Europe and the Americas.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

Role: Staff Engineer (Integrations / Supply, air travel)
Company: Voyagu
Location: Fully remote, Europe preferred. European time zone; about two hours of difference is fine. About eight hours online, and some overlap with US time zones helps because many users are there.
Job Type: Full-time. Contract model is flexible: contractor, payroll provider or direct employment.
About Voyagu
Voyagu builds one platform that runs several travel businesses. Today the focus is air travel. The platform covers client management (CRM), ERP modules for finance and accounting, travel operations, and integrations with travel supply systems.
The model is offline travel: agencies that sell through people. Voyagu does not sell the software and does not plan to, but agencies work with it in different models. It is a bootstrap scaleup, so teams are lean and money is counted.
Development leans heavily on AI. Teams of AI agents run big features under a business operator and a technical operator. Sometimes this turns two half-years of work into two weeks. It does not always work. When code is cheap, product vision and architecture become the bottleneck, and that is where you come in.
This role owns the integrations and supply direction. Air travel alone is deep: every airline has its own distribution channels and APIs. You would lead one of five platform development streams and report to the CTO. There is no product manager in between, and you work directly with the founder and other business stakeholders. The team has no one with your profile today, so you would be the first.
What you are expected to do
Technical ownership
• 
Lead the integrations and supply direction as its technical owner.
• 
Build integrations with GDS systems. Voyagu works with one today and needs more.
• 
Connect airline direct APIs and non-GDS protocols across multiple sources.
• 
Handle servicing after sale: changes, cancellations, refunds, and group bookings split into parts.
• 
Work with live, real-time availability. Seat availability does not depend on price.
• 
Prevent costly errors. One missed booking can mean tens of thousands of dollars. Design for reliability, for example with idempotency, so nothing is paid or bought twice.
• 
Keep the solution sized to Voyagu’s scale and avoid over-design. This is not internet-scale work.
• 
Keep the system stable. Speed and error rate are the measures.
Vision and delivery
• 
Shape the technical vision with stakeholders and defend it. They will challenge it.
• 
Expect no ready-made tasks. Business stakeholders give you a direction, not a finished task.
• 
Turn the agreed platform capabilities into features and give estimates. Several dozen capabilities are written down, such as search and booking.
• 
Success means Voyagu accepts your estimates and you deliver them, or come close. Part of the plan will be agreed together with you.
AI-driven development
• 
Build and direct teams of AI coding agents instead of writing code by hand.
• 
Explain and defend how to use AI effectively.
• 
Bring AI practices that are as good as Voyagu’s, or better.
Team
• 
Lead the two people already working in this direction, once you have onboarded.
• 
Hire as little as possible. Hiring is a last resort. Long term the direction may grow to one to three people.
What you need to succeed
• 
You have worked in the travel domain, especially on integrations with supply systems. About two or more years is likely enough.
• 
You understand booking versus ticket, and the statuses and states of each.
• 
You have owned a large piece of a product, not a small slice.
• 
You work at staff or senior level, as architect and technical lead.
• 
You understand what Voyagu does and why, and you talk well with stakeholders.
• 
You use AI well beyond the beginner level and have a clear view on how to use it effectively.
• 
You believe small teams work. You do not think in big organisations.
• 
You work in a European time zone; ideally you are based in Europe.
• 
You speak Russian: engineering works mostly in Russian. Business teams speak English, and English B2 is enough.
• 
Nice to have: you have seen both corporate and lean startup worlds, or a bootstrap scaleup. You may be an ex-founder or a small-company CTO who stayed hands-on.
• 
Nice to have: you have run teams of agents, not only asked an agent to write a feature.
• 
Nice to have: vendor-side experience building for end users. Python is the current main stack, but language skill is not important.
• 
Not required: high-load experience, writing agent skills, or deep C#/legacy aviation knowledge.
What you get
• 
You own a whole direction, with responsibility handed over fully.
• 
You are the technical lead for integrations and supply, with no product-manager layer in between.
• 
You work with AI agent teams. Voyagu will invest heavily in tokens and compute where it pays off.
• 
You can bring AI practices better than Voyagu’s own, and the team will share theirs.
• 
A large, technically hard platform: real-time inventory, many sources, money at stake.
• 
A lean environment with few meetings and flexible hours.
• 
Fully remote in Europe, with flexible contract models.
• 
Equity is not standard, but it is negotiable for an exceptional candidate.
How to apply
Apply through hirehire, the agency running this search for Voyagu. The process has three stages: an engineering interview with the CTO, a travel-domain interview with the founder, and a practical case with a defence.
